domain.title: Programming fundamentals
domain.summary: The building blocks every program is made of: data, control flow, functions, state, errors, modules, and asynchronous work.

concepts.title: Values and types
concepts.summary: Programs manipulate values; types describe which values are allowed and which operations make sense on them.

related.boundary: Validating external data at runtime maps there; what the language's types guarantee maps here.

learningObjectives: Distinguish primitive values from structured values such as objects and arrays
Explain why static type annotations and assertions are erased at runtime, and contrast them with runtime checks
Predict the result of common type coercions, numeric edge cases (NaN, floating-point rounding), and nullability checks
recognitionSignals: type assertions or non-null assertions (`as`, `!`, `as unknown as`) that override the checker
runtime conversions such as `Number()`, `parseInt`, `String()`, or `Boolean()`, and their failure values (NaN, empty string)
loose equality (`==`) or truthiness checks applied to values that may be 0, empty string, null, or undefined
nullable fields or optional values newly introduced or narrowed (`T | null`, Option/Maybe, nil checks)
discriminated unions or enums narrowed with typeof/instanceof/tag checks
misconceptionPatterns: Believing static type annotations still exist or are checked when the program runs
Treating null, undefined, empty string, and zero as interchangeable
Assuming a type assertion such as `as` converts a value rather than only silencing the type checker
Believing floating-point numbers represent decimal amounts such as 0.1 or currency exactly

concepts.title: Control flow
concepts.summary: Conditionals, loops, and early returns decide which statements run and in what order.
learningObjectives: Trace which branch of a conditional executes for given inputs
Explain how early returns and guard clauses change the reachable paths through a function
Identify off-by-one and non-terminating loop conditions
recognitionSignals: deeply nested or newly added conditional branches that change which path runs
switch/match over an enum or union without a default or exhaustiveness check
loop bounds or termination conditions (`<=` vs `<`, index arithmetic, while loops with a manual exit)
guard clauses with early return, continue, or break that skip later code
misconceptionPatterns: Assuming a JavaScript/C-style switch case without break stops at the end of that case
Believing a chain of conditionals covers every input when some inputs match no branch
Believing `if (value)` skips only null or undefined, when it also skips 0, empty string, and false

concepts.title: Functions and calls
concepts.summary: Functions package behavior behind parameters and return values; calling one creates a new frame of execution.
learningObjectives: Trace arguments into parameters and return values back to the caller
Explain the call stack and what happens when a function calls another
Distinguish pure functions from functions with side effects
recognitionSignals: changes to a function's parameters, defaults, or return type that affect its callers
functions with some code paths that return nothing (implicit undefined/None)
functions passed as arguments or returned as values (callbacks, handlers, strategies)
a function that both computes a result and performs side effects such as I/O or logging
misconceptionPatterns: Believing a block-bodied function such as `function f() { x + 1 }` or `() => { x + 1 }` returns its last expression, as a concise arrow body would
Assuming a function with side effects returns the same result every time it is called with the same arguments

concepts.title: Scope and closures
concepts.summary: Scope determines which names are visible where; closures let functions keep access to variables from where they were created.
learningObjectives: Predict which binding a name refers to in nested scopes
Explain how a closure captures variables rather than values
Recognize stale-closure and module-level shared-state bugs
recognitionSignals: functions returned from or defined inside other functions
UI hooks or effects that capture props or state (e.g. React useEffect or useCallback)
module-level variables mutated by functions
event handlers or timers referencing outer variables
misconceptionPatterns: Believing a closure snapshots a variable's value when created, rather than keeping a live reference to the variable
Believing a callback created in an earlier render or call sees later state, when it closed over a binding that was replaced rather than reassigned
Assuming module-level state is per request on a server
Confusing block scope with function scope (e.g. `var` in loops shared across iterations)

concepts.title: Mutation and references
concepts.summary: Some values are shared by reference; changing them in one place changes them everywhere they are referenced.
learningObjectives: Predict when two variables refer to the same underlying object
Explain the difference between shallow and deep copies
Evaluate when immutability prevents a class of bugs
recognitionSignals: push, splice, sort, reverse, or direct property assignment on objects or arrays received from elsewhere
functions that modify their object or array arguments
spread syntax, structuredClone, or copy helpers used before modifying data
an existing object or array mutated and then passed to a state setter, cache, or store
readonly modifiers, Object.freeze, or immutable data structures
misconceptionPatterns: Believing spread syntax performs a deep copy
Assuming const makes an object immutable
Believing sort or reverse return a new array and leave the original unchanged
Assuming passing an object or array to a function gives the function its own copy

concepts.title: Error handling
concepts.summary: Errors signal that an operation could not complete; handling them well means deciding where to recover, report, or propagate.
learningObjectives: Trace how a thrown error propagates up the call stack
Distinguish expected failures from programming bugs
Evaluate whether a catch block recovers, translates, or silently hides a failure
recognitionSignals: try/catch/finally blocks
custom error classes, result types, or errors returned as values (`if err != nil`, `Result`)
catch blocks that log and continue, return a default, or are empty
errors rethrown or wrapped, with or without the original cause
misconceptionPatterns: Believing catching an error means the failure was handled
Believing that throwing a new error in place of the original loses nothing useful for debugging
Assuming finally only runs on success

concepts.title: Modules and boundaries
concepts.summary: Modules group related code behind an explicit interface so the rest of a program depends on what it exports, not how it works.
learningObjectives: Explain what a module's public interface is and why it should be small
Predict module initialization order and side effects at import time
Evaluate whether a dependency direction between modules makes sense
recognitionSignals: a new module, or a change to what an existing module exports
barrel/index files that re-export other modules
top-level code that runs on import (opening connections, reading env, registering handlers)
imports that reach into another module's internal files instead of its entry point
circular imports between files
misconceptionPatterns: Assuming importing a module has no side effects
Treating every exported symbol as a stable contract by accident
Believing circular imports are always harmless

concepts.title: Synchronous vs. asynchronous work
concepts.summary: Asynchronous code starts work that finishes later, letting a program wait on I/O without stopping everything else.

related.boundary: Running several operations at once, and the races that creates, maps there.

learningObjectives: Explain what it means for a program to wait on network or disk work
Predict execution order around await, promises, and callbacks
Identify an un-awaited promise and its consequences for errors and ordering
recognitionSignals: calls to async functions whose promise is not awaited, returned, or handled (floating promises)
async callbacks passed to APIs that ignore the returned promise, e.g. `array.forEach(async ...)` or event emitters
manually constructed promises or futures, promisify, or then/catch chains mixed with await
callback-style I/O APIs
misconceptionPatterns: Believing await blocks the whole process
Believing a surrounding try/catch will catch the rejection of a promise that is never awaited
Believing `forEach` or similar callback APIs wait for async callbacks to finish before continuing

concepts.title: Dates, times, and time zones
concepts.summary: An instant in time, a calendar date, and a local wall-clock time are different things; confusing them causes off-by-hours and off-by-a-day bugs.
learningObjectives: Distinguish an instant (UTC timestamp) from a calendar date and a local wall-clock time
Predict how a date is parsed, displayed, or compared across server and client time zones
Explain where time-zone conversion should happen when storing and displaying times
recognitionSignals: new Date(), Date.now(), or date parsing from strings
toISOString, toLocaleString, or date-library formatting and time-zone calls
timestamp vs timestamptz or date columns in schemas
date arithmetic such as adding days, start/end of day, or expiry comparisons
misconceptionPatterns: Believing a date-only string such as "2024-03-10" is parsed in local time by JavaScript's Date
Assuming every day has 24 hours in local time
Believing storing local time without a zone preserves the moment an event happened
